correctness.rationale: For x<a both classes require link 1, and for x>b both require link 2, contradictions. In (a,b) only E uses link 1 and therefore x=theta; at a exactly a-theta time drivers must use link 1, feasible iff theta<=a, and at b exactly b emissions drivers use link 1, feasible iff theta>=b. This determines both class flows, including zero-demand classes and ties. Writing e1(x)-e2(1-x)=(v+z)(x-b) gives G=w+z+(v+z)[x^2-(b+rho)x]. Projecting its vertex s=(b+rho)/2 onto the attainable interval [a,b] proves the strict wedge, both equality plateaus, and the endpoint savings. Independent rational evaluation gave 21/5, 15/4, 21/5, hence 9/20 twice. Replay the independent spot check with python /workspace/branches/independent-algebra.py (item 2); neither this check nor sampling proves the general result.

originality.rationale: The qualitative possibility of a mixed optimum, class-specific equilibrium conditions, and generic parallel-network uniqueness are not new. These follow from a direct two-link sign reduction and objective minimization, not by substituting into a known stronger classification. value.rationale: The mathematical gap is motivated independently of the example: a primary two-link study avoided mixed demand for multiplicity reasons. The complete share classification shows when neither pure-policy comparison can find the optimum, gives both exact losses, and distinguishes that case from the plateaus. It resolves a practical question within a clean static model without claiming field calibration, heterogeneous congestion effects, or a network-level policy forecast.
